**Meeting.** Troy School District Board of Education, regular meeting, 7:00 p.m., Tuesday, May 19, 2020, by Zoom (Meeting ID 248 952 1600; dial-in 253-215-8782 or 301-715-8592). District address 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.4000. Public comment is limited to one-half hour for agenda items and one-half hour for non-agenda items, three minutes per speaker.

**Recognitions.** Fourteen nominees for the 2019-20 Outstanding Support Staff Award, with Barb Pangle, secretary at Hill Elementary School, named Overall TSD Outstanding Support Staff / Employee of the Year; retirees honored included Peter Maurer (Baker Middle, dedicated employee since 1978); and a resolution supporting National Teacher Appreciation Week, May 4-8, 2020.

**Consent agenda (items A-G).** Minutes of the April 14, 2020 special meeting and workshop and the April 21, 2020 special workshop and regular meeting; the March 2020 Treasurer's Report; approval of the Oakland Intermediate School District budget; and a resolution to hold a public hearing on the proposed 2020/2021 budget. April 14 actions: Resolution 20-039 ratifying the March 27, 2020 tentative agreement with the Troy Education Association/MEA/NEA for February 1, 2020 through January 31, 2021, and Resolution 20-040 adopting a COVID-19 Mitigation, Self-Reporting, Leave of Absence policy under existing policy 1000.03. April 21 actions: Resolution 20-042, sale of 6.12 +/- acres on the north side of Square Lake Road east of John R Road to Robertson Brothers Homes for $1,425,000.00 with $50,000.00 earnest money (Yes 5, No 2 - Gottlieb, Hammond); Resolution 20-043, Niles Demolition to International Construction, Inc., $356,385.00; Resolution 20-044, Niles casework to Advanced Building Group, $161,300.00; Resolution 20-045, Troy College and Career High School furniture, $96,390.54.

Consolidated debt service revenues $16,669,502 against $16,447,590 budgeted, expenditures $2,721,787 of $17,740,610. Consolidated special revenue revenues $7,698,116 of $10,981,040. Consolidated capital projects revenue $14,029,388 against an $8,848,080 budget (158.56%), expenditures $13,830,753 of $23,061,248.

**Oakland Schools FY 2020-21 proposed budget** (transmittal letter of March 24, 2020 from Superintendent Dr. Wanda Cook-Robinson). Property tax revenue growth projected at 3.25%, with a Headlee rollback of the operating millage possible. Literacy Essentials Oakland is a four-year, $5 million pre-K through 3rd grade initiative across all 28 constituent districts. PA-18 base special education distribution is budgeted to increase approximately $10.0 million, or 7.9%, plus $3.5 million for other LEA distributions; $3.39 million above base was distributed in FY 2019-20. Personnel: step increases plus a 1.0% across-the-board increase; retirement rate rising from 27.5% to 28.21% on October 1, 2020, blended rate projected at 28.0%.

**Other items.** Item 5.G sets a public hearing on the 2020-2021 budget for June 16, 2020 at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois Road. Items 7.A and 7.B recommend Goodheart-Wilcox secondary health materials totaling $123,041 for 2020-21, unanimously endorsed by the Sex Education Advisory Board on April 30, 2020. Item 8.A awards aluminum storefront/glazing for the Niles Relocation Project to Advanced Building Group at $111,882.00 from the 2020 Capital Projects Fund. Item 10.A supports Mr. George Ehlert for a six-year Oakland Schools board term ending June 30, 2026, elected June 1, 2020. Item 10.B casts Troy's votes for Dr. Robert Shaner and Mark Dziatczak as at-large members of the International Academy governing body. Item 10.C is Dr. Machesky's COVID-19 report, 'A Look Ahead.'

## Meeting and notice

Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting, Tuesday, May 19, 2020, 7:00 p.m., by Zoom (Meeting ID 248 952 1600; dial-in 253-215-8782 or 301-715-8592), district offices at 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.4000. Public comment is limited to one-half hour for agenda items and one-half hour for non-agenda items, three minutes per speaker. Board members: Anne, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff, Philippart, Schmidt and Wilson, with Gary N. Hauff as Secretary, Superintendent Dr. Machesky and Rick West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services.

## Recognitions

Fourteen individuals were nominated for the 2019-20 TSD Outstanding Support Staff Award; Barb Pangle, secretary at Hill Elementary School, was named Overall TSD Outstanding Support Staff / Employee of the Year. Retirees recognized included Peter Maurer (Baker Middle, dedicated employee since 1978), Janis Sattler-Fried (Speech Pathologist, 1978), Sharon Callas (1981) and Donna Giannetti (1995); Jordan Harris read the names. A resolution supported National Teacher Appreciation Week, May 4-8, 2020.

## Consent agenda (items A-G) and prior minutes

The April 14, 2020 special meeting (5:45 p.m. to 6:04 p.m.) heard Troy High junior Ammar Ahmad ask for letter grades rather than credit/no credit. Resolution 20-039 ratified the March 27, 2020 tentative agreement with the Troy Education Association/MEA/NEA for February 1, 2020 through January 31, 2021; Resolution 20-040 adopted the COVID-19 Mitigation, Self-Reporting, Leave of Absence policy, waiving a first reading under policy 1000.03 and expiring December 31. The April 14 workshop ran 6:05 p.m. to 9:21 p.m. and the April 21 special workshop 6:03 p.m. to 6:53 p.m., with Dana Abrahams of Clark Hill, PLC present.

At the April 21, 2020 regular meeting (7:05 p.m. to 8:20 p.m.), forty-four teachers were nominated for the Outstanding Teacher Award, with Carolyn Maher (Wass), Amanda Fisher (Larson) and Jeff Rainwater (Troy College and Career High School) sent to Oakland Schools. Resolution 20-041 approved the consent agenda (Yes 7, No 0). Resolution 20-042 authorized sale of 6.12 +/- acres of vacant land on the north side of Square Lake Road east of John R Road, part of a 70.647 +/- acre Parcel 2, with an 11.281 +/- acre Parcel 1 preserved by conservation easement, to Robertson Brothers Homes for $1,425,000.00 with $50,000.00 earnest money; Yes 5, No 2 (Gottlieb, Hammond). Resolutions 20-043, 20-044 and 20-045 awarded Niles Demolition to International Construction, Inc. at $356,385.00, Niles casework to Advanced Building Group at $161,300.00, and Troy College and Career High School furniture at $96,390.54, each Yes 7, No 0.

## Item 5.F - Oakland Intermediate School District 2020-2021 budget

Section 624 of the Revised School Code requires the ISD to submit its proposed budget by May 1 and each constituent board to adopt a resolution of support or disapproval by June 1. Troy expresses support while stating that its support is for the sole purpose of complying with Section 624 and that the Intermediate School District is responsible for its own operations, including adoption of its budget. The transmittal letter of March 24, 2020 from Superintendent Dr. Wanda Cook-Robinson projects growth in Oakland Schools property tax revenues of 3.25%, tempered by a possible Headlee rollback of the operating millage measured against the Consumer Price Index. Literacy Essentials Oakland, prompted by declining 3rd grade M-STEP reading levels, is a four-year, $5 million pre-K through 3rd grade initiative with all 28 constituent districts. The CTE allocation to LEAs was increased by more than 25% in 2019-20 and continues in 2020-21. Shared services cover technology for thirteen (13) districts and business office services for five (5); Illuminate Education has served all twenty-eight (28) districts and two (2) public school academies since Fall of 2016 with a 50% subsidy again in 2020-21. Personnel costs carry step increases plus a 1.0% across-the-board increase; the Basic/MIP with Health Care Premium Subsidy retirement rate rises from 27.5% to 28.21% on October 1, 2020, with a blended rate projected at 28.0%. Health care hard caps are $18,596.96 family, $14,260.37 individual plus one and $6,818.87 single after 1/1/20, projected at $19,154.87, $14,688.18 and $7,023.44 after 1/1/21 assuming medical price index growth of 3.0%. PA-18 base special education distribution is budgeted to increase approximately $10.0 million, or 7.9%, with $3.5 million more for group homes, startup, extraordinary expenditures and capital, following $3.39 million above base in FY 2019-20.

## Item 5.G - public hearing on the proposed 2020-2021 budget

State law requires a hearing noticed at least six (6) days in advance, the notice carrying in 11-point bold faced type the statement that the property tax millage rate proposed to be levied to support the proposed budget will be a subject of the hearing. The resolution sets the hearing for June 16, 2020 at a special Board meeting beginning at 7:00 p.m. at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois Road, or via Zoom; Exhibit A, signed by Gary N. Hauff, states 5:00 p.m. Budget copies are available at 4400 Livernois, June 3 through June 16, 2020.

## Items 7.A and 7.B - secondary health materials

Presented by Natalie Haezebrouck, Director of Teaching and Learning, under the district's regular nine-year adoption cycle; the health team first met in September of 2019. Both teams recommended Goodheart-Wilcox: Essential Health Skills for Middle Schools, Second Edition and Comprehensive Health Skills, Third Edition by Catherine Sanderson and Mark Zelman, each with a nine-year online subscription to the G-W Learning Platform and Schoology integration; preview access used username troyhealth, password troyhealth21, 4/7/2020 to 6/24/2020. The Sex Education Advisory Board met April 30, 2020 at 6:30 PM with Oakland Schools consultant Christina Harvey and voted unanimously to approve the textbooks. The total cost of these materials is $123,041 for the 2020-21 school year.

## Item 8.A - Niles relocation aluminum storefront

Memorandum of April 29, 2020 from Rob Carson, Director of Maintenance and Operations, to Rick West on BP 29A, Niles Relocation Project, 1140 Rankin. RFP 9908 re-bid exterior aluminum storefront, doors and hardware after the original package drew no bids. Two proposals were received April 14, 2020: Modern Mirror & Glass Co. at $77,150, which omitted the specified electrified hardware, and Advanced Building Group at $111,882, recommended as low qualified bidder by Barton Malow Company in a letter from Steven L. Rewers. The resolution awards Advanced Building Group $111,882.00 from the 2020 Capital Projects Fund.

## Item 10.A - Oakland Schools biennial election

Under Public Act 419 of 2004 and MCL 380.614, intermediate board members are elected biennially on the first Monday in June by an electoral body of one designee per constituent district, on a resolution adopted not earlier than 21 days before the election. Troy supports Mr. George Ehlert for the one (1) position, a term of six (6) years ending June 30, 2026, directing its representative to vote for him at least on the first ballot. Filing closed May 1, 2020 and resolutions were due May 29, 2020; balloting is in person 5:30-7:30 PM June 1, 2020 at the Oakland Schools Conference Center, 2111 Pontiac Lake Road, Waterford, with no absentee ballots and oath of office July 7, 2020. The March 25, 2020 cover letter is from Barb DeMarco, Secretary, Oakland Schools Board of Education, and a May 4, 2020 email from Nicole Christian notes Mr. Ehlert is the only filed candidate; the statute sets a nonrefundable $100.00 filing fee in lieu of petitions.

## Item 10.B - International Academy governance

At its October 2, 2019 meeting the International Academy Joint Steering Committee approved amending the governance structure so the Consortium is governed by a five-member body of the representatives of its three Fiscal Agents plus two at-large members elected by all Participating Districts for two-year terms. The only two districts whose boards adopted ballot resolutions were Rochester Community Schools (Dr. Robert Shaner) and Birmingham Public Schools (Mark Dziatczak); Troy casts its vote for both.

A slide report by Dr. Machesky on the impact of COVID-19, listing frozen unnecessary spending, adjusted budgets, urgent priorities and furloughed staff.
